A thin sheet, either perforated or using some other technique, with which a pattern may be produced upon a surface; a utensil that contains a perforated sheet.

examples.text: You do not necessarily need to have a stencil brush to paint over a stencil.

glosses: A pattern produced using such a utensil.

examples.text: In 2013 a damaged stencil of a rat and an image of a girl hugging a bomb were painted over on the walls of a Fitzroy church by the building owner’s father-in-law, who tried to help out by painting the building while house sitting. He did not know the significance of the stencils.

examples.text: Stencilled letters were used for words and phrases, as well as for captions for some of his stencil “prints,” print being used in the sense of a multicolor woodcut.

A physical object whose shape is used as a guide to make other objects.
A generic model or pattern from which other objects are based or derived.

examples.text: Gaelic also benefits from having a readily available template for Celtic minority language revitalisation, derived from Welsh and Irish.

glosses: A file or document serving as a basis for others.
A macromolecule which provides a pattern for the synthesis of another molecule.

examples.text: Classically, the functional product of coding genes is a protein whose synthesis is directed by an mRNA-template.

glosses: A partially defined class or function, that can be instantiated in a variety of ways depending on the instantiation arguments.
A strip of metal used in boiler-making, pierced with a series of holes, and serving as a guide in marking out a line of rivet-holes.
Synonym of temple.

examples.text: The template length is adjusted to the proper fabric width. Then the sharp pins in the template ends are hooked into the selvedge edges (with the template open).

glosses: To set up or mark off using a template.

examples.text: Only that part of the floor timber that bears on the planking and keel need be templated; […]

glosses: To provide a template or pattern for.

examples.text: Metal phosphates that are templated by transition-metal complexes are rare.

glosses: To synthesize by means of a template.
